label: ADHD-like traits reshape the balance between inhibitory control and predictive processes
summary: n = 226 non-clinical sample; Cognitive Trade-off Task measuring response inhibition and statistical learning simultaneously; ADHD traits measured dimensionally with the ASRS v1.1.

label: Annual Research Review: Categories versus dimensions in the classification and conceptualisation of child and adolescent mental disorders
venue: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, 53(5):469–489
summary: Canonical review of the category-vs-dimension question in child psychopathology; summarises the ADHD taxometric studies (Haslam 2006, Marcus & Barry 2011) and concludes ADHD is best modelled as a continuum.

label: Understanding attention deficit hyperactivity disorder as a continuum
summary: Clinician-facing review arguing ADHD lacks a taxon; neuropsychological performance varies linearly with symptom load with no discontinuity, creating uncertainty about where any intervention threshold should sit.

label: Does Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Have a Dimensional Latent Structure? A Taxometric Analysis
summary: Taxometric analysis of the NICHD sample finding a dimensional latent structure for inattention, hyperactivity/impulsivity and ADHD overall, with stronger validity than dichotomous models.

label: Genetics of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
summary: Review of ADHD genetics; twin and molecular evidence that clinical ADHD is the extreme of a continuous, heritable distribution with shared aetiology across the full symptom range.

label: Discovery of the first genome-wide significant risk loci for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder
summary: First well-powered ADHD GWAS; strong concordance with GWAS of quantitative population symptom measures supports clinical ADHD as an extreme expression of continuous heritable traits.

label: The World Health Organization Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS): a short screening scale for use in the general population
summary: Development of the ASRS; optimal scoring is an unweighted symptom sum (a dimensional score), with a 6-item Part A retained as a fast screener.

label: SWAN Scale for ADHD Trait-Based Genetic Research: A Validity and Polygenic Risk Study
venue: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, 60(9):988–997
summary: Validates the SWAN, a symmetric strengths-to-weaknesses rating that yields roughly normally distributed ADHD-trait scores; argues dichotomising a continuous trait into case/control loses statistical power.

label: The Factor Structure of ADHD – Different Models, Analyses and Informants in a Bifactor Framework
venue: Journal of Psychopathology and Behavioral Assessment, 39(1):92–102
summary: Supports a bifactor structure for ADHD: a dominant general factor plus weak specific inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity factors.

label: Research Domain Criteria (RDoC): Toward a New Classification Framework for Research on Mental Disorders
summary: Founding RDoC commentary; reorganises psychopathology around functional dimensions studied across their full range, including executive- and impulse-control constructs central to ADHD.

label: The Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP): A Dimensional Alternative to Traditional Nosologies
summary: Dimensional classification framework that places ADHD within the (disinhibited) externalizing super-spectrum rather than as a discrete category.

label: The p Factor: One General Psychopathology Factor in the Structure of Psychiatric Disorders?
summary: Finds psychopathology is best captured by a single general 'p' dimension paralleling g; ADHD loads via the externalizing pole, reinforcing a graded liability model.

label: Is ADHD a Dimension or a Category? What Does the Relationship Between ADHD Traits and Psychosocial Quality of Life Tell Us?
summary: Psychosocial quality of life declines linearly with ADHD-trait level, with no non-linear breakpoint at the high end — direct support for a dimensional model over a category.

label: Subthreshold Autism and ADHD: A Brief Narrative Review for Frontline Clinicians
summary: Narrative review synthesising taxometric, impairment and threshold evidence; documents that sub-threshold ADHD carries wide-ranging functional impairment relative to unaffected peers.

label: Overdiagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Scoping Review
summary: Scoping review of 334 studies finding convincing evidence that ADHD is overdiagnosed; for milder cases the harms of diagnosis may outweigh the benefits — a caution against unbounded threshold-lowering.

label: Childhood attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder as an extreme of a continuous trait: a quantitative genetic study of 8,500 twin pairs
venue: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, 53(1):73–80
summary: Flagship twin study reporting near-identical group heritability at diagnostic and screening cutoffs — ADHD as the quantitative extreme of a continuous trait.

label: Dimensional and Categorical Approaches to Understanding Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: New Frontiers in Translational Research
venue: Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, 3(8):652–653
summary: Counter-point to the dimensional consensus: reports taxometric outcomes more consistent with a categorical structure within ADHD samples and a dimensional structure in typically developing groups.

label: The factor structure of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in schoolchildren
venue: medRxiv preprint (later Research in Developmental Disabilities)
summary: Reports the latent correlation between the inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity factors (0.78 school / 0.68 clinical) and finds a bifactor model — strong general factor plus weak specific factors — fits best.

label: Practitioner Review: Do performance-based measures and ratings of executive function assess the same construct?
venue: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, 54(2):131–143
summary: Review of 20 studies finding rating-based and performance-based measures of executive function correlate only weakly (median r = .19) and assess different underlying constructs.

label: Causal heterogeneity in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: do we need neuropsychologically impaired subtypes?
summary: Argues that group neuropsychological deficits in ADHD reflect only a subgroup — for any given mechanism, only a subset of behaviourally defined cases is impaired.

label: Beyond the dual pathway model: evidence for the dissociation of timing, inhibitory, and delay-related impairments in ADHD
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, 49(4):345–355
summary: Finds inhibitory, temporal-processing and delay-related deficits are independent neuropsychological components whose co-occurrence in ADHD is no greater than chance — dissociable pathways.

label: Reaction time variability in ADHD: a meta-analytic review of 319 studies
summary: Meta-analysis establishing greater reaction-time variability in ADHD (g = 0.76 children, 0.46 adults) while showing it is not specific to ADHD relative to other clinical groups.

label: The clinical utility of the continuous performance test and objective measures of activity for diagnosing and monitoring ADHD in children: a systematic review
summary: Systematic review finding mixed, non-decisive evidence for using continuous performance tests to support ADHD diagnosis and medication decisions.

label: A review of the validity of laboratory cognitive tasks used to assess symptoms of ADHD
summary: Concludes that even the best-supported cognitive tasks (CPT, choice-delay, stop-signal) need further validation before use beyond experimental purposes.

label: Validity of the executive function theory of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a meta-analytic review
summary: Landmark meta-analysis: executive-function deficits in ADHD are of moderate effect size and not universal — neither necessary nor sufficient.

label: A comprehensive assessment of memory, delay aversion, timing, inhibition, decision making and variability in ADHD
summary: For each cognitive domain, only a minority of children with ADHD (roughly 18–36%) show a deficit — quantifying neurocognitive heterogeneity across six pathways.

label: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder and Monetary Delay Discounting: A Meta-Analysis of Case-Control Studies
venue: Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, 1(4):316–325
summary: Meta-analysis finding individuals with ADHD discount delayed monetary rewards more steeply than controls — the motivational/reward pathway.

label: A review of behavioural rating scales for the assessment of ADHD among adults in research
summary: Reviews adult ADHD rating scales (incl. CAARS, BAARS-IV); notes scales should not be the sole basis for diagnosis and that combining interviews, CPTs and scales maximises accuracy.

label: Diagnosing ADHD
venue: CHADD — National Resource Center on ADHD (CDC cooperative agreement)
summary: Patient-facing clinical guidance stating there is no single test for ADHD and that a comprehensive, multi-source evaluation is required.

label: Unraveling the optimum latent structure of ADHD: evidence supporting ICD and HiTOP frameworks
summary: Locates ADHD within HiTOP as dimensions (inattention, hyperactivity, impulsivity) under the disinhibited externalizing spectrum rather than as a single category.

label: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis: Clinical Utility of Continuous Performance Tests for the Identification of ADHD
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, 63(2):154–171
summary: Meta-analysis: CPTs differentiate ADHD from non-ADHD only modestly (pooled sensitivity 0.75, specificity 0.71) and should be used only within a comprehensive diagnostic process.

label: ADHD and behavioral inhibition: a meta-analytic review of the stop-signal paradigm
summary: Meta-analysis finding that stop-signal differences in ADHD reflect a generalized attention/processing deficit rather than a specific behavioural-inhibition failure.

label: Are we measuring ADHD or anxiety? Examining the factor structure and discriminant validity of the ASRS in an adult anxiety disorder population
summary: In an adult anxiety sample, several ASRS hyperactivity items loaded more strongly onto anxiety than ADHD; the scale captured non-ADHD symptoms and is susceptible to over-reporting.

label: Is adult ADHD a childhood-onset neurodevelopmental disorder? Evidence from a four-decade longitudinal cohort study
summary: Dunedin birth cohort: childhood-ADHD and adult-ADHD groups were virtually non-overlapping, and the adult group showed neither childhood neuropsychological deficits nor polygenic risk for childhood ADHD.

label: Evaluation of the persistence, remission, and emergence of ADHD in young adulthood
summary: E-Risk twin cohort: 67.5% of young adults with ADHD had never met criteria in childhood; the late-onset group had higher childhood IQ and fewer externalizing problems.

label: ADHD trajectories from childhood to young adulthood: evidence from a birth cohort supporting a late-onset syndrome
summary: Pelotas birth cohort: only 17.2% of childhood cases persisted and only 12.6% of adult cases had childhood ADHD; the authors propose two syndromes with distinct trajectories.

label: Late-onset ADHD reconsidered with comprehensive repeated assessments between ages 10 and 25
summary: Using eight repeated multi-informant assessments, ~95% of screen-positive late-onset cases were excluded on careful diagnosis; survivors are reframed as late-identified rather than late-onset.

label: Variable patterns of remission from ADHD in the Multimodal Treatment Study of ADHD
summary: Across 16 years, only 9.1% recovered and 10.8% were stably persistent; 63.8% showed fluctuating persistence and remission, motivating a person-environment fit framework.

label: ADHD in DSM-5: a field trial in a large, representative sample of 18- to 19-year-old adults
summary: Supports five inattention symptoms as the optimal adult cut-off while estimating a 27% increase in expected young-adult prevalence from DSM-IV to DSM-5.

label: The prevalence of adult attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder: a global systematic review and meta-analysis
summary: Persistent adult ADHD 2.58% vs symptomatic adult ADHD 6.76% — a ~2.6x difference driven purely by whether childhood onset is required; both decline with age.

label: ADHD diagnosis, treatment, and telehealth use in adults — National Center for Health Statistics Rapid Surveys System
venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, 73(40):890–895
summary: 6.0% of US adults had a current ADHD diagnosis in 2023; 55.9% were diagnosed at age 18 or older — late identification is the majority pathway.

label: Sex and age differences in ADHD symptoms and diagnoses: implications for DSM-V and ICD-11
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, 49(3):217–228
summary: Community-ascertained male:female ratio of 2.28:1, well below clinic-based ratios, indicating females are underdiagnosed in the community.

label: Sex differences in predicting ADHD clinical diagnosis and pharmacological treatment
summary: Swedish cohort: diagnosed ratio 2.5:1 vs symptom-criteria ratio 1.8:1; externalizing behaviour drives referral, and females are missed without it.

label: Annual Research Review: ADHD in girls and women — underrepresentation, longitudinal processes, and key directions
venue: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, 63(4):484–496
summary: Reviews presentation differences, the narrowing adult sex ratio, compensation/masking, and the male-referenced bias of ADHD symptom lists.

label: The prevalence of DSM-IV attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a meta-analytic review
summary: The inattentive presentation is most common in the population, but combined-type individuals are more likely to be referred for services — a structural referral filter.

label: Gender differences in objective and subjective measures of ADHD among clinic-referred children
summary: Documents the 2:1 to 10:1 range of reported sex ratios and that higher ratios come specifically from clinical rather than population-based samples.

label: Bias by gender: exploring gender-based differences in the endorsement of ADHD symptoms and impairment among adult patients
summary: Notes that only 21% of participants in the DSM-5/ICD-11 ADHD field trials were girls, so diagnostic tools were largely not designed with women in mind.

label: Modeling attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a critical appraisal of the cognitive-energetic model
summary: Argues inhibition deficits in ADHD may be partly explained by energetic (activation/effort) dysfunction, while conceding the model needs direct measures of the energetic pools.

label: A comparison of two models of ADHD: state regulation versus delay aversion
venue: Doctoral dissertation, Ghent University (ch. based on Metin et al. 2012, Biological Psychiatry 72:990–996)
summary: Meta-analysis of event-rate effects showing ADHD performance deficits are condition-dependent; also states that the energetic pools are affected by stress, sleep-wake cycle and noise.

label: Arousal dysregulation and executive dysfunction in attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
summary: Reviews evidence that the ADHD impairment is in the ability to self-regulate arousal rather than a constant under- or over-aroused state, while noting mixed results.

label: Mind wandering perspective on attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
summary: Proposes that altered default-mode deactivation and DMN–executive interaction produce excessive spontaneous mind-wandering underpinning ADHD symptoms.

label: Validation of the Mind Excessively Wandering Scale and the relationship of mind wandering to impairment in adult ADHD
summary: Validates the MEWS (sensitivity .9, specificity .9) and finds mind-wandering contributes to impairment independently of core ADHD symptom dimensions.

label: Mind-wandering, depression, anxiety and ADHD: disentangling the relationship
summary: Found no mind-wandering difference between ADHD and non-ADHD groups; mind-wandering tracked anxiety instead and 'cannot be considered a hallmark of ADHD'.

label: Associations of sleep disturbance with ADHD: implications for treatment
venue: ADHD Attention Deficit and Hyperactivity Disorders, 7(1):1–18
summary: Sets out four modes of ADHD-sleep interaction including that sleep problems may cause or mimic ADHD, and notes no experiment has shown sleep restriction induces hyperactivity.

label: Impact of sleep extension and restriction on children's emotional lability and impulsivity
summary: In healthy children with no sleep or behavioural problems, ~54 minutes of cumulative sleep restriction produced detectable deterioration on blinded teacher ratings.

label: Sleep restriction and extension in adolescents with ADHD
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, 58(4):433–442
summary: Experimental evidence that sleep duration is a causal contributor to daytime behaviour in adolescents with ADHD; hyperactivity-impulsivity was lower under restriction.

label: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in adults: evidence base, uncertainties and controversies
summary: Comprehensive review of adult ADHD; sets out onset, trajectory and mechanism as the three tests for differential diagnosis, and describes adult hyperactivity as inner restlessness.

label: Inhibitory control and psychopathology: a meta-analysis of studies using the stop signal task
venue: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society, 16(6):1064–1076
summary: Medium stop-signal deficits across ADHD (g=0.62), OCD (g=0.77) and schizophrenia (g=0.69) — inhibition impairment is transdiagnostic, and OCD's exceeds ADHD's.

label: The Internal Restlessness Scale: performance of college students with and without ADHD
summary: Develops the Internal Restlessness Scale (IRS) to measure the mental/subjective restlessness that adults with ADHD report in place of overt motor hyperactivity; ADHD college students score significantly higher, and the scale shows a four-factor structure.

label: Practical considerations for the evaluation and management of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in adults
summary: Clinician-facing review of adult ADHD; notes that in adulthood hyperactivity is more often internalized and that inattention can be masked by anxiety or obsessive-like compensation — directly relevant to the internal-restlessness / anxiety differential.

label: The Internal, External, and Diagnostic Validity of Sluggish Cognitive Tempo: A Meta-Analysis and Critical Review
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, 55(3):163–178
summary: First meta-analysis of sluggish cognitive tempo (SCT): across >19,000 individuals 13 SCT items load on an SCT factor separable from ADHD; SCT correlates more with internalizing than with hyperactivity/impulsivity and predicts impairment — evidence for a construct distinct from ADHD inattention.

label: Report of a Work Group on Sluggish Cognitive Tempo: Key Research Directions and a Consensus Change in Terminology to Cognitive Disengagement Syndrome
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, 62(6):629–645
summary: Consensus paper renaming SCT to cognitive disengagement syndrome (CDS); defines it as cognitive disengagement/decoupling of attention (staring, daydreaming, mental fogginess) plus hypoactivity, empirically distinct from ADHD inattention and linked to depression, with data across the lifespan.

label: The prevalence and correlates of adult ADHD in the United States: results from the National Comorbidity Survey Replication
summary: Nationally representative US survey (NCS-R): current adult ADHD prevalence 4.4%, highly comorbid with other DSM-IV disorders and substantially impairing; most cases untreated though often treated for the comorbidities — evidence the disorder frequently hides behind its co-occurring conditions.

label: Emotion dysregulation in attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
summary: Review concluding emotion dysregulation is prevalent across the ADHD lifespan and a major source of impairment, arising from attention-to-emotion deficits in a striato-amygdalo-medial-prefrontal network; explicitly lays out three competing models of how it relates to ADHD (distinct dimension / core feature / separate entity).

label: Adult ADHD and comorbid disorders: clinical implications of a dimensional approach
summary: Review of adult ADHD comorbidity: up to 80% have a coexisting psychiatric disorder (most often mood/anxiety), overlapping symptoms complicate diagnosis, and a spectrum/dimensional framing plus treat-the-most-impairing-first is advocated; emotional dysregulation described as a distinctive attribute of adult ADHD.

label: A conceptual review of the comorbidity of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and anxiety: implications for future research and practice
summary: Conceptual review of ADHD–anxiety comorbidity (~25% of children with ADHD have an anxiety disorder); examines methodological and substantive causes including temperament, genetics and the temporal relations between the two, and argues progress needs more precise phenotypic classification of ADHD.

label: The World Federation of ADHD International Consensus Statement: 208 Evidence-based conclusions about the disorder
summary: Consensus statement (79 authors, 27 countries) distilling ADHD evidence into 208 numbered conclusions; Conclusion 14 states ADHD can only be diagnosed by a licensed clinician via interview and not by rating scales, neuropsychological tests or imaging alone.

label: Updated European Consensus Statement on diagnosis and treatment of adult ADHD
summary: European consensus (63 experts) on adult ADHD assessment and treatment: the clinical interview is essential and covers childhood and adult symptoms/impairment; a collateral informant is of great value where retrospective recall is poor; a four-symptom adult cut-off is endorsed.

label: Accuracy of adult recall of childhood attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
summary: Prospective 16-year follow-up testing whether adults accurately recall childhood ADHD: positive predictive value of retrospective self-report was only 0.27, so most retrospective childhood diagnoses are invalid — underscoring the need for contemporaneous or collateral childhood information.

label: When diagnosing ADHD in young adults emphasize informant reports, DSM items, and impairment
venue: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 80(6):1052–1061
summary: Childhood-diagnosed sample (N=321) showing parent report is more diagnostically sensitive than self-report: young adults with ADHD underreport symptoms while controls overreport, with no added benefit to combining self-report with parent report — argues for weighting informants and impairment.
